name: C

image.dockerfile:
FROM debian:trixie-slim
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends gcc g++ make libc6-dev && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

conventions: C17 compiled with `-std=c17 -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all`, so memory errors and UB fail the run. The code under test is `solution.h` + `solution.c` in starter/, solution/ and every bugs/<name>/ (the header is identical in all). `tests/Makefile` compiles `test.c` with `-I../$(TARGET) ../$(TARGET)/*.c` into a binary under /tmp and runs it (copy the Makefile from the example). `tests/test.c` uses the CHECK macros from the example: each check prints `[ok]   <name>` or `[FAIL] <name>` with expected/got, and main prints `ALL TESTS PASSED` only when there are zero failures (exit 1 otherwise). `bugs[].expect` is the failing check's name. The starter must COMPILE under -Werror (silence unused parameters with `(void)param;`) and return a wrong placeholder. Teach ownership: document who frees what in solution.h.

levelNotes.1: Strings and arrays with explicit lengths; no dynamic allocation needed yet.
levelNotes.3: Introduce malloc/free with clear ownership, struct APIs, size_t arithmetic.
levelNotes.5: Good depth topics: dynamic arrays with growth strategy, intrusive linked lists, parsing with strtol and errno, bit manipulation.
levelNotes.7: Good depth topics: arena/pool allocators, hash tables with open addressing, function pointers for generic containers.
